state.task:
Question-answering task using the company document service.

The company handbook is held by a document service; it is not available as files. Documents
have a header line (version, status, effective dates, what they supersede) and numbered
sections; each section is a passage, cited as "HB-07 §2". Documents can have superseded
versions, and memos can add group exceptions and carve-outs. Use the rule that applies to the
situation and date in the question.

Service actions (reply with one of these instead of "execute"):
  {"action": "search", "query": "lodging limit Geneva", "k": 5, "thought": "..."}
      up to k (at most 8; default 5) ranked passages with ids and document headers. Each
      result is also saved under /task/workspace/search-results/ (path in the result header),
      where your code can read it later.
  {"action": "fetch", "ids": ["HB-07 §2", "HB-12"], "thought": "..."}
      the named passages in full; a document id ("HB-12") returns all its sections; at most
      10 ids per fetch.
You can still use "execute" for code (for example to read saved results or manage your
context), and "final" to answer.

Questions:
- Q1: What is the paid sick days for an employee with twelve years of service on a fixed-term contract today? (answer in days per year)
- Q2: What is the flight fare limit for a standard return flight within Europe with checked equipment today? (answer in EUR per return flight)
- Q3: What is the paid parental leave for an employee who is the primary carer of a newborn today? (answer in weeks)
- Q4: What is the relocation lump sum for a regular employee relocating at the company's request today (2026-10-13)? (answer in EUR)
- Q5: What is the purchase approval threshold for a regular department's purchase from a supplier with a framework contract today? (answer in EUR)
- Q6: What bike-leasing allowance applied to a regular employee leasing a commuter bike on 2026-03-15? (answer in EUR per month)

Finish with {"action": "final", "answer": {"answers": [{"question": "Q1", "value": "...",
"citations": ["HB-07 §2", ...]}, ...]}}. Give one entry per question. The value must be the
exact amount; citations must include every passage needed to support it (for example the rule
and any exception or carve-out that applies), not just one passage.
state.step_intent: Find the flight fare limit that applies to: What is the flight fare limit for a standard return flight within Europe with checked equipment today?

passages.source: HB-65 §2 | Travel policy: flights — Standard flight fare limit | version: 3 · status: current · effective: 2026-05-01 · supersedes: HB-62
passages.text: The flight fare limit for an economy return flight is 300 EUR. The travel office publishes worked examples of the flight fare limit on the intranet. The travel office reviews the flight fare limit once a year and announces changes in advance.

passages.source: HB-62 §2 | Travel policy: flights — Standard flight fare limit | version: 2 · status: superseded · effective: 2025-01-01 to the day before 2026-05-01 · superseded by: HB-65
passages.text: The flight fare limit for an economy return flight was 350 EUR. Each claim for the flight fare limit needs a receipt showing the date, the amount and the supplier. Questions about the flight fare limit go to the travel office, who keeps the record of decisions.

passages.source: HB-60 §1 | Memo: flight fare limit exceptions — Purpose | version: 1 · status: current · effective: 2025-01-01
passages.text: This memo lists group exceptions to the flight fare limit in HB-65. The travel office publishes worked examples of the flight fare limit on the intranet. Questions about the flight fare limit go to the travel office, who keeps the record of decisions.

passages.source: HB-60 §2 | Memo: flight fare limit exceptions — Exception for intercontinental flights | version: 1 · status: current · effective: 2025-01-01
passages.text: For intercontinental flights, the flight fare limit is 1000 EUR per return flight instead of the standard amount. Managers confirm claims for the flight fare limit before payment in the next payroll run. The travel office reviews the flight fare limit once a year and announces changes in advance.

passages.source: HB-60 §3 | Memo: flight fare limit exceptions — Carve-out | version: 1 · status: current · effective: 2025-01-01
passages.text: The exception above does not apply to flights booked by contractors; they follow the standard flight fare limit in HB-65 §2. Managers confirm claims for the flight fare limit before payment in the next payroll run. The travel office reviews the flight fare limit once a year and announces changes in advance.
